evidence.claim: Old King's Highway is a 34-mile National Scenic Byway through a Cape Cod landscape of marsh views, cranberry bogs and stretches framed by trees.
evidence.quote: National Scenic Byway • Massachusetts Length 34 mi / 54.7 km

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration highlights its combination of scenery and historic buildings: the drive passes through eight National Register districts, with early Cape houses, sea captains' homes and Victorian buildings along the way.
evidence.quote: This roadway is a major tourist attraction due to its scenic and historic attributes, as well as its proximity to Cape Cod beaches and recreational attractions. A trip down this roadway takes the traveler through America’s largest historic district and eight National Register districts, and past dozens of National Register buildings, including early Cape Cod houses, sea captains’ homes, and Victorian buildings.

evidence.claim: In Barnstable, this was the principal east-west road, linking the town's main population centers from the late 1630s.
evidence.quote: The Old King's Highway Historic District encompasses what was historically the principal east–west thoroughfare through Barnstable, Massachusetts.

evidence.claim: As maritime business shifted toward the southern villages in the early 19th century, construction along the old highway declined. That slowdown left a concentration of Federal and Greek Revival buildings.
evidence.quote: Because of the shift of Barnstable's economy to more maritime concerns based in villages along its southern coast beginning in the early 19th century, the villages along the King's Highway gradually declined in economic importance, with a resultant decline in construction.  As a result, the district has a large number of Federal and Greek Revival properties.

evidence.claim: The Route 6A number came later: it first appeared between Bourne and Barnstable in 1953 as the Mid-Cape Highway opened, then extended toward Orleans in 1956.
evidence.quote: Route 6A was first signed upon partial completion of the Mid-Cape Highway, which was Cape Cod's first freeway in 1953, traveling between the Sagamore Bridge in Bourne and Route 132 in Barnstable.

evidence.claim: Traveling east, the road leads from Bourne through Sandwich to Barnstable, then Yarmouth and Dennis before reaching Brewster and Orleans.
evidence.quote:
Bourne:  Sandwich Road
Sandwich:  Route 6A
Barnstable:  Main Street
Yarmouth:  Main Street
Dennis: Old King's Highway
Brewster:  Main Street
Orleans:  Cranberry Highway

evidence.claim: In Brewster, Route 6A becomes Main Street through the town center; Drummer Boy Park holds the Old Higgins Farm Windmill beside the route.
evidence.quote: The Drummer Boy Park on Route 6A has walking trails, picnic areas, playground, and an 18th-century windmill, the Old Higgins Farm Windmill, and blacksmith shop.

evidence.claim: At Orleans, Routes 6A and 28 join before ending at the Route 6 rotary on the Eastham town line.
evidence.quote: The two routes join in the Orleans town center and end at a rotary with Route 6 at the Eastham town line.

evidence.claim: Sandwich's glass industry left a neighborhood as well as glassware. Deming Jarves founded the Boston & Sandwich Glass Factory in 1825; its lead glass became known for its color.
evidence.quote: Deming Jarves founded the Boston & Sandwich Glass Factory in 1825. Sandwich had proximity to a shallow harbor, was a possible canal site, and had local supplies of timber to fuel the furnaces. The glass works primarily made lead glass and was known for its use of color.

evidence.claim: In Jarvesville, most of the historic district's contributing properties are homes built between 1825 and 1860, when the company was at its height. Modest Cape and Greek Revival houses sheltered glassworkers.
evidence.quote: most of the district's more than 200 contributing properties are residences built between 1825 and 1860, when the glass company was at its height.  These houses are predominantly Cape and Greek Revival in character, and are modest one- and two-family buildings that originally housed glass factory workers.

evidence.claim: The industrial buildings were eventually demolished in the 20th century. The houses continued to be occupied, including by glassworkers' descendants and workers from other industries.
evidence.quote: the industrial properties were eventually demolished in the 20th century.  The residential properties continued to be occupied, often by descendants of the glassworkers, but also by workers employed in other industrial facilities in the area.

evidence.claim: The old county courthouse on Route 6A became a place of resistance on September 27, 1774. Protesters demanded that county officials refuse to obey the Massachusetts Government Act, which had stripped the colony of rights of self-government. The officials agreed, effectively ending royal control of the county.
evidence.quote: The 1763 county courthouse, at 3046 Rt. 6A, was the scene of a historic mass protest on Sept. 27, 1774, against British efforts to punish Massachusetts for the Boston Tea Party the previous year. The protesters demanded that county officials refuse to obey the Massachusetts Government Act, passed by the British Parliament in May 1774, which stripped the colony of its long-held rights of self-government. County officials agreed, and Royal control of the county effectively ended.

evidence.claim: The building later changed purposes: in 1842 it was remodeled for the Third Barnstable Baptist Church. After that congregation disbanded in 1972, the nonprofit Tales of Cape Cod purchased it. This is one of two remaining Massachusetts colonial courthouses where the 1774 protests took place.
evidence.quote: The Barnstable building is one of only two remaining Massachusetts colonial-era courthouses where those 1774 protests were mounted.

evidence.claim: in 1842 it was remodeled for the Third Barnstable Baptist Church. After that congregation disbanded in 1972, the nonprofit Tales of Cape Cod purchased it.
evidence.quote: The old courthouse was remodeled in 1842 to serve as a home for the newly formed Third Barnstable Baptist Church. After the church was disbanded in 1972, the building was purchased by Tales of Cape Cod, a nonprofit volunteer group committed to preserving the Cape's history.

evidence.claim: Brewster's sea captains helped shape the town's architecture. Wealthy captains and commercial businessmen built Italianate, Greek Revival and Second Empire homes here during the 19th century.
evidence.quote: Architecturally, Brewster blossomed during this period, with wealthy sea captains and commercial titans constructing Italianate, Greek Revival, and Second Empire homes.

evidence.claim: The town's surviving captains' houses include the Cobb House of 1799, now home to the Brewster Historical Society.
evidence.quote: Brewster is known as the "Sea Captain's Town" for its wealth of eighteenth and nineteenth century historic captain's homes, including the Cobb House (1799), the current home of the Brewster Historical Society.

evidence.claim: There is another kind of working history at Drummer Boy Park on Route 6A: the Old Higgins Farm Windmill dates to 1795. The park also has a blacksmith shop and walking trails. Along the town's northern shore, the Brewster Flats spread out as tidal sand flats on Cape Cod Bay.
evidence.quote: Old Higgins Farm Windmill (1795)

evidence.claim: The park also has a blacksmith shop and walking trails.
evidence.quote: The Drummer Boy Park on Route 6A has walking trails, picnic areas, playground, and an 18th-century windmill, the Old Higgins Farm Windmill, and blacksmith shop.

evidence.claim: Along the town's northern shore, the Brewster Flats spread out as tidal sand flats on Cape Cod Bay.
evidence.quote: The town is bordered by the Brewster Flats, an extensive stretch of tidal sand flats to the north, along the shores of Cape Cod Bay.

evidence.claim: Barnstable Village remained the county’s civic center as its economic importance declined.
evidence.quote: Barnstable Village stretched out along the highway remained the civic administrative center of the county
